toil as an MCP server

Running toil as an MCP server over stdio, the tools and resources it serves, and registering it with Claude Code, Codex, VS Code and other clients

Docs / toil as an MCP server

toil mcp serves every toil command as an MCP tool over stdio. It’s the same core as the CLI, with the same inputs and the same envelope. A tool’s name is its command path with underscores: toil jira get-issue is jira_get_issue. It never opens a network port.

  • --areas jira,confluence serves exactly those areas, so an agent sees a short tool list and one server entry stands in for one vendor’s server. Commands outside an area are areas of their own here: add version or connections to the list to serve them too. Without --areas, toil serves every area that has a connection set up, plus every command that needs none (version, connections list, jira schema).
  • Writes: a write tool is listed only when one of its area’s connections has writes: true, and every call still needs allowWrite: true. Deletes, and the commands that prompt or change connections (connections add, setup alias), are never tools.
  • Files: a command that reads or writes a file needs a workspace: `—workspace ` in the server's args, else `TOIL_WORKSPACE`, else the client's root when it shares exactly one. With none, it returns `NOT_CONFIGURED`.
  • wait: the wait tool repeats one read tool until a condition over its data holds (SKILL.md describes it). It’s served whenever a read tool is, --areas or not, and repeats only the tools the server serves. After every attempt that doesn’t end the wait it sends a progress notification when the call carried a progress token, so a client that resets its tool-call timeout on progress keeps a long wait alive. The notifications are checked with the MCP TypeScript SDK’s client (resetTimeoutOnProgress), and the Codex CLI ran a one-minute wait to its end. Whether Claude Code, Codex or other clients reset their own tool-call timeout on progress hasn’t been checked, so with those keep timeout under the client’s tool-call limit.
  • Progress: any tool call that carried a progress token also gets a progress notification for each page a listing reads and each rate-limited (429) request toil waits to retry, with the same message the CLI writes to stderr (core.md, Progress). The envelope is the same either way.
  • Resources: besides tools, the server serves read-only resources that describe toil’s own context, so a client can read it without a tool call. None reads from a service, and none holds a secret. They follow --areas as the tools do.
    • toil://connections: each connection’s name, area, isDefault and writes, for the areas served. Never a host or a credential.
    • toil://dossiers and toil://dossiers/<name>: what the dossiers_list and dossiers_show tools return, served when those tools are.
    • toil://skill/<area>: this skill’s page for each area served, such as toil://skill/jira for jira.md.
  • Config: the server reads ~/.toil/config.json, or --config <file> in its args, and the TOIL_* env vars it is started with. Keep tokens in the OS credential store (toil connections add, run once on a terminal) rather than in the client’s env block, which is a file someone may share or commit.

Registering it

The examples use toil on PATH and the Jira area; change --areas to what the task needs.

Claude Code

claude mcp add toil -- toil mcp --areas jira

Codex

codex mcp add toil -- toil mcp --areas jira

or in ~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.toil]
command = "toil"
args = ["mcp", "--areas", "jira"]

VS Code and GitHub Copilot, in .vscode/mcp.json:

{ "servers": { "toil": { "type": "stdio", "command": "toil", "args": ["mcp", "--areas", "jira"] } } }

Claude Desktop, Cursor and other clients with an mcpServers file:

{ "mcpServers": { "toil": { "command": "toil", "args": ["mcp", "--areas", "jira"] } } }

When toil isn’t on PATH

MCP clients start servers without a shell, so they don’t read shell profiles and a toil alias doesn’t apply. Use one of these as the command and its args instead:

Installedcommandargs
From a clonenode["<clone>/dist/toil.js", "mcp", "--areas", "jira"], with the clone’s absolute path
Not at all, once toil is on npmnpx["-y", "@imagile-dev/toil", "mcp", "--areas", "jira"]
From npm, on Windowscmd["/c", "toil", "mcp", "--areas", "jira"], because npm’s toil.cmd needs a shell to start

In JSON and TOML, write a Windows path with forward slashes (C:/Users/you/toil/dist/toil.js), which Node accepts.

Checking it works

Ask the agent to list toil’s tools and call one that needs no connection: version (served when --areas is left out or names version) returns the same envelope as toil version, { "ok": true, "data": { "version": … } }. A tool that isn’t listed is in an area --areas leaves out, in an area with no connection set up (without --areas), or a write tool on a connection without writes: true.
